title: Reconstructing the Spatial Audio Effect's Spatial Indexing Layer
topic: How I reverse engineered a commercial spatial audio effect

abstract: Spatial audio engines embed high-dimensional positional data within proprietary data structures that are opaque to reverse engineers. This work dissects a commercial effect by reconstructing its spatial indexing layer in C\#. We identify a balanced search tree that satisfies the height-balance and key-ordering invariants of an AVL-style structure, enabling logarithmic point and range queries. Formal invariants are proven using an automated AST inspection pipeline that verifies the tree's structural bounds. The resulting implementation achieves $O(log N)$ search and insertion, matching the theoretical limits of balanced spatial indexes such as Stratum-Analytics-Trees \cite{Guttman_1984_RTrees} and KD-Trees \cite{Bentley_1975_KDTree}. The source code is publicly available for reproducibility. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/csharp-enterprise-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261011_170108_how_i_reverse_engineered_a_com}
